'''Orbot''' is a [[Free software|free]] [[Proxy server|proxy]] [[Mobile app|app]] that provides [[anonymity]] on the [[Internet]] for users of the [[Android (operating system)|Android]] and [[iOS]] [[operating system]]s. It allows traffic from apps such as web browsers, [[email]] clients, map programs, and others to be routed via the Tor network.<ref name="ehack">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ehacking.net/2011/04/orbot-tor-anonymous-on-android.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110418185427/http://www.ehacking.net/2011/04/orbot-tor-anonymous-on-android.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=18 April 2011|access-date=21 July 2012|publisher=[[eHacking.net]]|title=Orbot: Tor- Anonymous on Android|first=Irfan|last=Shakeel|date=April 2011}}
</ref>

This tool is used to keep the communications of users anonymous and hidden from governments and third parties that might be [[2010s global surveillance disclosures|monitoring their internet traffic]].<ref>{{Cite web|access-date=21 July 2012|title=From encryption to darknets: As governments snoop, activists fight back|first=Cyrus|publisher=[[Ars Technica]]|last=Farivar|date=15 February 2012|url=https://arstechnica.com/business/the-networked-society/2012/02/from-encryption-to-darknets-as-governments-snoop-activists-fight-back.ars}}</ref>

== Reception ==
In 2014 Orbot was discussed in detail in an article on "reporting securely from an Android device".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Advice for reporting securely from an Android device|url=https://ijnet.org/fr/node/3302|access-date=2021-08-22|website=Réseau international des journalistes|language=fr}}</ref> In January 2016, Lisa Vaas of NakedSecurity by Sophos described how to use Tor, including with Orbot on Android, to connect to [[Facebook]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vaas |first=Lisa |date=2016-01-21 |title=Facebook users get support for safe browsing with Tor on Androids |url=https://nakedsecurity.sophos.com/2016/01/21/facebook-users-get-support-for-safe-browsing-with-tor-on-androids/ |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=Naked Security |language=en-US |archive-date=2 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230202093453/https://nakedsecurity.sophos.com/2016/01/21/facebook-users-get-support-for-safe-browsing-with-tor-on-androids/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In July 2021, Tech Radar named Orbot one of 8 "Best privacy apps for Android in 2021" but warned of slower speeds.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Drake|first=Nate|date=2021-07-28|title=Best privacy apps for Android in 2021|url=https://www.techradar.com/best/best-privacy-apps-for-android|access-date=2021-08-22|website=TechRadar|language=en}}</ref> In July 2021 Android Authority discussed Tor Browser and Orbot in brief reviews of "15 best Android browsers".<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-29|title=15 best Android browsers for surfing whatever website you want|url=https://www.androidauthority.com/best-android-browsers-320252/|access-date=2021-08-22|website=Android Authority|language=en-US}}</ref>

In November 2021, John Leyden of The Daily Swig described collaboration between the Tor Project and [[Guardian Project (software)|the Guardian Project]] to develop Orbot for censorship circumvention for any application on a device, but warned Orbot does not remove identifying information from app traffic.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-11-18 |title=Tor Project unveils plans to route device traffic through Tor anonymity network with new VPN-like service |url=https://portswigger.net/daily-swig/tor-project-unveils-plans-to-route-device-traffic-through-tor-anonymity-network-with-new-vpn-like-service |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=The Daily Swig {{!}} Cybersecurity news and views |language=en}}</ref> In July 2022, Laiba Mohsin of PhoneWorld.com described Orbot as a simple way to access the [[Dark web|Dark Web]] on mobile.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mohsin |first=Laiba |date=2022-07-06 |title=What Is Dark Web & How To Access It? |url=https://www.phoneworld.com.pk/what-is-dark-web-how-to-access-it/ |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=PhoneWorld |language=en-US}}</ref>

In October 2022, Damir Mujezinovic of MakeUseOf described Orbot as a "flagship" product for both iOS and Android to use the Tor network, and said it "will not make you completely anonymous, but it can certainly help bypass certain geographical restrictions,"<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mujezinovic |first=Damir |date=2022-10-27 |title=The 5 Best Free Apps to Strengthen Your Smartphone's Security |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/free-apps-boost-smartphones-security/ |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=MUO |language=en}}</ref> In November 2022, Mujezinovic wrote a detailed guide to using Orbot on iOS or Android.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mujezinovic |first=Damir |date=2022-11-07 |title=How to Access Tor on Your Smartphone |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/use-orbot-access-tor-smartphone/ |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=MUO |language=en}}</ref>
